subject: Why won't all the modification indices show up? No ~1 is showing.

messages.author: 90e03273c83a92f7
messages.subject: Why won't all the modification indices show up? No ~1 is showing.
parts:
I don't get it...I have a simple 2 factor model, and I'm doing multi-group CFA so I have a 0/1variable called "millennial" which I use to define my groups. I run a full measure equivalence model as follows:


fit2 <- cfa(model,data=GSS, group = "millennial",group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts"))
fitMeasures(fit2, selected)

modindices(fit2)


But from the modindices() function I only am shown modification indices of type =~ and ~~ but not ~1. I need the ~1 MIs so that I know which intercepts to free! Why is it not showing them?

This group seems to have no trouble getting them to show up even though our syntax is identical (slide 26)

http://users.ugent.be/~yrosseel/lavaan/multiplegroup6Dec2012.pdf

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Why won't all the modification indices show up? No ~1 is showing.
parts: But from the modindices() function I only am shown modification indices of type =~ and ~~ but not ~1. I need the ~1 MIs so that I know which intercepts to free! Why is it not showing them?

Because you are already estimating all of your intercepts.  The modIndices() function only returns indices for parameters that are fixed to a certain value (e.g., zero).  If you want indices to test equality constraints, use the lavTestScore() function.  You can compare the constraints in the output to those in the parTable() or summary() output to see how to adjust your syntax.  You can read more details I posted here:

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/lavaan/l5aUQfvcZT4/S_uGCAhICAAJ

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

When I estimate the model for my groups individually, all the parameters are pretty similar.

The biggest discrepancy is the intercept estimates for my variable marhomo: 2.0 vs 2.7 (standardized its 1.5 vs 1.8). 

My variable abany on the other hand is estimated at 1.5 (3 when standardized) for both groups.

by FAR the biggest chi-square is due to setting abany (p19/p45) equal!! marhomo meanwhile are p18/p44. 

So sure enough, if I set that intercept free my model fit statistics go insanely high, CFI/TLI are .99 and I drop lots of chi-square. The intercepts for abany are now 1.5 (3 if standardized) and 1.7 (3.5 standardized).

How on earth does that work? Does this probably mean I'm fundamentally doing something else wrong? For the record, imposing measurement equivalence only raised the chi-square from 33 to 35. Thank you in advance for any help!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Why won't all the modification indices show up? No ~1 is showing.
parts: When I estimate the model for my groups individually, all the parameters are pretty similar.

I wouldn't compare multigroup results to separate single-group results.  You can already compare parameters in a multigroup configural model because there are no across-group equality constraints.  I imagine those parameter estimates are nearly identical to the ones from your separate single-group models.

I think a more relevant question is what the intercepts look like in the metric-equivalence model (only loadings are constrained to equality across groups, and only 1 group's factor variances are fixed for identification).  In that model, it makes sense to compare intercepts because the factor loadings are parallel across groups, so the distance between those regression lines is the same for any level of the latent factor (think of the homogeneity of slopes assumption in ANCOVA).  In the configural model, those lines are not necessarily parallel, so the intercept is just an arbitrary level of the latent factor (usually in the middle because the means are fixed to zero for identification), but the mean difference between groups can vary across levels of the latent factor.

Of course, if that is the case, the test of metric equivalence should have failed first, and I'm guessing that curious item with the "same" intercepts but a high modification index probably should not have its loadings constrained -- in which case there would be no logic to constraining their intercepts either.  From your description (7 indicators of 2 factors), I'm not sure why you have only 8 equality constraints from the scalar-equivalence model.  If you post your R syntax and some relevant output, it might be clearer what you are doing.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
